_about: Public documentation authority map - the declaration side of the single-authority check.

The enforcing contract (required topics, sentinel phrases, forbidden files) is hard-coded in the CI quality job and in scripts/check-docs-local.mjs; this file declares the same mapping in a readable, reviewable form, so deleting a topic or weakening a sentinel here cannot switch the check off.
sentinel = structural phrases that must appear in the authority file and must not appear in forbidden_in files; must_link = files that must carry a markdown link to the authority.

install.why: Install steps, platform choice and reset behaviour live in one place; the entrance page shows the three-step path and links here for everything else.

workflow.why: The node list, the per-node lifecycle and the real entry points are the product contract; other files summarise and link.

troubleshooting.why: Recovery advice is only usable when it is grouped by symptom in one place.

release.why: Version semantics, the version record surfaces and the release checklist drifted once already (five steps vs seven); contributors are sent here instead of a second copy. The sentinel phrases stay count-free on purpose: one that carries the count breaks as soon as the count is corrected.

behaviour.why: The guarantees and the custom-protocol material form one contract; a second statement elsewhere would be a second contract.

contributing.why: Contribution rules, including what may be borrowed from the upstream project, belong with the contributor flow.

sentinel: All notable changes to this project
history.why: Per-version history stays in the changelog; other surfaces link to it.

upstream.why: The short statement of the upstream relationship belongs on the entrance page only.

security.why: Vulnerability reporting has a single home by convention, and the entrance page must point at it.

counts.policy: Scenario and item counts may appear only on the README badge line and in the release authority; every other public surface says see VERSIONS instead of repeating a number.

internals.policy: Implementation-internal identifiers (hook script names, bridge loader file names, hook payload fields, machine-owned state field names) belong to the internal surfaces only. The two command entry scripts users actually run - workflow-state.mjs and workflow-guard.mjs - are command surface, not internals, and may appear in public documents.
